canonical_statement: The study examined whether cefazolin could serve as an empiric alternative to vancomycin in a freestanding chronic hemodialysis population and evaluated postdialysis cefazolin pharmacokinetics to determine dose and frequency.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the spectrum of infectious complications from a large outpatient hemodialysis center was examined to determine the role that cefazolin might have as an empiric antibiotic

canonical_statement: The retrospective susceptibility analysis came from a freestanding outpatient hemodialysis center with a census of 217 patients observed for 7 months.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a freestanding (ie, not hospital-associated) outpatient hemodialysis center with a census of 217 patients were examined during a 7-month period

population.label: freestanding outpatient chronic hemodialysis center population

canonical_statement: The pharmacokinetic component included selected chronic hemodialysis patients with clinical infection and cefazolin-susceptible positive cultures; all included patients were anuric.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin was given to selected chronic hemodialysis patients who had a clinical infection and a positive bacterial culture indicating in vitro sensitivity to cefazolin. All patients were anuric.

population.label: selected anuric chronic hemodialysis patients with clinical infection and cefazolin-susceptible positive culture

canonical_statement: All non-urine cultures were categorized by source, Gram stain category, and susceptibility to cefazolin, vancomycin, cefazolin plus gentamicin, and vancomycin plus gentamicin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All non-urine cultures were categorized by location (blood or wound), Gram’s stain (gram-positive, gram-negative, or other), and sensitivity to cefazolin, vancomycin, cefazolin plus gentamicin, and vancomycin plus gentamicin.

canonical_statement: Urine cultures were excluded from the susceptibility analysis because urinary tract infections were considered rarely treated with parenteral antibiotics in this setting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: urine cultures were excluded from further analysis

population.label: non-urine cultures from the outpatient hemodialysis center

canonical_statement: The culture review did not determine whether positive cultures represented true clinical infection, colonization, or contamination.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No determination was made as to whether positive cultures represented true clinical infection, colonization, or contamination.

canonical_statement: A wound-culture subset was constructed by excluding likely nonpathogens; clinically significant cultures were defined as positive blood cultures plus wound cultures containing probable pathogens.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a subset of wound cultures excluding nonpathogenic organisms was developed

canonical_statement: Cefazolin was administered intravenously over 5 minutes after dialysis as 1 g for 11 dose observations or 2 g for 4 dose observations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin was administered as a 1-g (n = 11) or 2-g (n = 4) dose over 5 minutes after dialysis.

canonical_statement: Dialysis during the pharmacokinetic study used an F80 polysulfone dialyzer, with clinical dialysis prescription parameters not altered for study purposes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dialysis was performed using an F80 polysulfone dialyzer. Blood flow rate, dialysate flow rate, time, and other components of the dialysis prescription were determined by clinical need and were not altered for the purposes of the study.

canonical_statement: Cefazolin concentrations were sampled around 15 doses for peak/trough analysis, around 15 dialysis treatments for pre/postdialysis analysis, and across 9 interdialysis periods for nondialysis clearance; BUN was measured before and after 14 dialysis treatments.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin levels were obtained before and 1 hour after 15 individual doses of cefazolin

canonical_statement: The investigators used classical pharmacokinetic formulas for volume of distribution, elimination rate constant, and half-life, and calculated urea reduction ratio and an analogous cefazolin reduction ratio.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Classical pharmacokinetic formulas were used to determine Ke and t1/2

canonical_statement: Susceptibility comparisons used chi-square testing; cefazolin versus urea removal used linear regression and categorical chi-square analyses, with P <= 0.05 considered statistically significant.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Statistical evaluation was done with chi-square analysis of sensitivity or resistance to each antibiotic and group of antibiotics within each culture category.

canonical_statement: Across 225 positive cultures, 19 cultures (8%) were MRSA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 225 positive cultures were obtained from a 217-patient, freestanding outpatient hemodialysis center over a 7-month period. MRSA was present in 19 cultures (8%).

population.label: all positive non-urine cultures

canonical_statement: For all 225 cultures, cefazolin covered 116 (52%) and vancomycin covered 165 (73%); cefazolin coverage was lower (P < 0.001).

population.label: all positive non-urine cultures

canonical_statement: For all 225 cultures, Table 1 reports 175 susceptible cultures for cefazolin plus gentamicin and 165 for vancomycin, with no statistically significant difference (P = 0.120); the printed percentage beside 175 is 50%.

canonical_statement: Using the Table 1 count, 175 of 225 cultures corresponds to 77.8% susceptibility to cefazolin plus gentamicin, not the printed 50%.

canonical_statement: For all 225 cultures, vancomycin plus gentamicin covered 212 (94%), which was higher than cefazolin plus gentamicin (P < 0.001).

canonical_statement: Among 18 blood cultures, cefazolin covered 14 (78%) and vancomycin 16 (89%); the difference was not significant (P = 0.371).

canonical_statement: The four blood cultures not covered by cefazolin were one MRSA, two enterococci, and one Bacteroides isolate; vancomycin would have missed both gram-negative bacteremias.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The organisms not covered by cefazolin include gram-positive MRSA (n = 1) and enterococcus (n = 2) and the gram-negative bacteroides (n = 1).

canonical_statement: Among 207 wound cultures, cefazolin covered 101 (49%) and vancomycin 150 (72%); cefazolin coverage was lower (P < 0.001).

canonical_statement: Vancomycin would have missed all 47 gram-negative wound cultures, whereas cefazolin alone covered 17 of 47 (36%).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Vancomycin would have missed all 47 of the gram-negative cultures, while cefazolin alone would have covered 17 (36%).

canonical_statement: Adding gentamicin to cefazolin expanded wound-culture coverage, including 7 of 18 MRSA, 16 of 44 Staphylococcus epidermidis, and 11 of 11 enterococcal isolates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The additional gram-positive organisms included seven of 18 MRSAs, 16 of 44 Staphylococcus epidermidis cultures, 11 of 11 enterococcus cultures

canonical_statement: Among 128 wound cultures classified as probable pathogens, cefazolin covered 73 (57%) and vancomycin 84 (66%); the difference was not significant (P = 0.158).

canonical_statement: Among 128 probable-pathogen wound cultures, cefazolin plus gentamicin covered 116 (91%) versus 84 (66%) with vancomycin (P < 0.001).

canonical_statement: Among 146 clinically significant cultures, cefazolin plus gentamicin covered 132 (90%) versus 100 (68%) with vancomycin (P < 0.001).

canonical_statement: Among 146 clinically significant cultures, vancomycin plus gentamicin covered 142 (97%) versus 132 (90%) with cefazolin plus gentamicin (P = 0.015).

canonical_statement: All study patients with clinical infections treated with cefazolin were reported to have clinically resolved their infections.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All patients with clinical infections treated with cefazolin clinically resolved their infections.

canonical_statement: One cefazolin-treated patient developed a morbilliform rash that resolved after cefazolin was discontinued.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: One patient developed a morbilliform rash that resolved with discontinuation of cefazolin.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: One patient developed a morbilliform rash.

canonical_statement: Table 2 listed drug acquisition cost and administration time as cefazolin $3.74/5 min, vancomycin $54.95/60 min, cefazolin plus gentamicin $7.69/35 min, and vancomycin plus gentamicin $58.90/90 min.
The authors estimated that replacing vancomycin with cefazolin would reduce drug acquisition costs by 93% for cefazolin alone and 86% for cefazolin plus gentamicin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Drug acquisition costs would decrease by 93% if cefazolin was used alone or by 86% if used with gentamicin.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that, in outpatient chronic hemodialysis facilities with low MRSA rates, empiric cefazolin could substitute for vancomycin for suspected infections on the basis of the observed in vitro susceptibility pattern.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Suspected infections in chronic hemodialysis patients receiving treatment at outpatient facilities with low rates of MRSA infection can be safely and effectively treated with empiric cefazolin in place of vancomycin.

canonical_statement: For cefazolin-susceptible infections in anuric hemodialysis patients, the authors recommended cefazolin 1 g intravenously after each dialysis session, without supplemental nondialysis doses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: cefazolin can be safely and effectively used at a dose of 1 g intravenously after each dialysis session. Nondialysis clearance is sufficiently low in anuric patients that supplemental doses are not needed.

canonical_statement: The authors recommended reducing the postdialysis cefazolin dose to 750 mg for patients weighing less than 50 kg to avoid potentially toxic peak concentrations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For patients weighing less than 50 kg, a reduced dose of 750 mg should be used to prevent potentially toxic levels.

canonical_statement: The postdialysis dosing recommendation was stated to apply only to anuric hemodialysis patients; a patient with significant residual urine output had substantially higher nondialysis clearance and low predialysis cefazolin concentrations and was excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The recommendation for postdialysis dosing is appropriate only for anuric hemodialysis patients.

canonical_statement: The pharmacokinetic study used only polysulfone dialyzers, and the authors stated that the effect of non-polysulfone membranes on cefazolin dose and frequency was unknown.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The current study was performed using only polysulfone dialyzers. Although cefazolin removal may be different with non-polysulfone dialysis membranes, the overall effect ... is unknown.

canonical_statement: The study did not measure cefazolin MICs and instead interpreted trough concentrations against an approximately 8 microg/mL susceptibility threshold referenced from NCCLS disk-sensitivity guidance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although the minimum inhibitory concentration of cefazolin was not measured in the current study, NCCLS guidelines indicate that disc sensitivity to cefazolin tends to correlate with a minimum inhibitory concentration of approximately 8.0 µg/mL.

canonical_statement: None of the cefazolin-treated study patients had bacteremia; bacteremic cefazolin treatment described after study completion was anecdotal and outside the prospective pharmacokinetic cohort.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although none of the study patients treated with cefazolin had bacteremia, since completion of the study, several patients with positive blood cultures have been treated with cefazolin.
